messages:
sam.green: Heads up — hit a reproducible KV cache memory creep on long chat sessions (>10k tokens). RSS climbs steadily across requests, not freed between turns.

nate.k: can you share the snapshots and how you repro?

sam.green: quick notes: resident goes 1.1G -> 1.62G after ~3k appends in our harness. jeprof points to allocator fragmentation; small free runs scattered across classes. Flame shows KV reserve + memcpy hotspots.

ravi.s: do we have a small reproducer? we should automate this for CI.

sam.green: yes — harness in infra/kv/bench/longrun. command: `./kv_longrun --clients 200 --append 800 --interval 4s --duration 7200s`. Will push config and CSVs.

joanne: what pattern exactly? which slot classes are failing?

sam.green: mostly 256B and 1KB slots are producing short free runs that can’t be used for 2–3KB-ish entries; allocator only frees whole blocks when empty so holes never coalesce. Over time holes fragment larger size needs and we keep allocating new blocks.

nate.k: obvious idea: background coalescer that merges adjacent free runs into the next size class. Needs to be low-impact.

ravi.s: agreed, but we need safe heuristics. propose: only run when kv.free_ratio < 0.15 and system tail latency below SLO. Also cap merges per-second and prefer idle cores.

joanne: sketch two modes: buddy-merge (safe, merges same-size adjacent runs) and run-length coalesce (merge multiple adjacent runs across sizes). Buddy is cheap and low-risk.

sam.green: implemented buddy-only prototype: `kv.coalesce.buddy`. POC result on harness: RSS slope changed from +420MB/hr -> +60MB/hr. CPU overhead ~0.7% on the bench workers.

nate.k: nice. what about latency spikes during merge ticks?

sam.green: baseline p99 30ms. with buddy coalescer at 1 merge/sec p99 33ms (we see small correlations). If we increase to 5/sec p99 edges up more. So default budget should be very conservative for hosted.

ravi.s: we should consider relocate as a follow-up: compact a partially filled block by moving live entries into another block and free the original, reducing fragmentation further. Relocate is memcpy-heavy and costs CPU but collapses holes proactively.

joanne: relocate plus coalescer could get us close to no-growth, but relocate increased p50 by ~3ms in sam’s microtest. For Dedicated we can allow more aggressive options, for Hosted keep relocate opt-in and gated.

sam.green: ran a relocate quick-run: mem growth dropped to ~8MB/hr but CPU went +3% and p99 increased to ~48ms. Tradeoffs clear.

nate.k: another lever — add a 2KB size class between 1KB and 4KB. From sample traces, a non-trivial fraction of entries sit around 1.3–2.2KB. Adding 2KB reduces cross-class allocations by ~10% in trace sim. Costs: more metadata and slightly higher internal fragmentation.

ravi.s: add the model numbers to the proposal. If we add 2KB we should also re-evaluate coalescer thresholds because smaller gaps will fit better.

joanne: metrics to emit: `kv.free_ratio`, `kv.buddy_merge_ops_total`, `kv.relax_relocate_ops_total`, `kv.merge_cpu_seconds`, and `kv.blockclass_count`. Also a tag `kv.coalesce_mode`. This will let us monitor both effectiveness and cost.

sam.green: checklist for PR (WIP at https://github.com/redwood-inference/kv/pull/701): unit tests for scanner/merge correctness, stress fuzz 48h with randomized sizes, SLA regression test (p99 < +10%), perf harness runs, and a 48h prod shadow. I attached harness CSVs and the jeprof outputs.

nate.k: add a controlled rollout plan: merge buddy coalescer behind a config flag default-on for Hosted but with tight budgets (0.5% CPU budget, 1 merge/sec max). Post-merge: 48h shadowing then enable for small percentage of traffic, monitor `kv.free_ratio` and p99. For Dedicated: provide config options to enable run-length coalesce and relocate with user CPU caps.

ravi.s: tests before merge: unit + fuzz, perf-ci overnight run with coalescer toggled, p99 SLA check, and validate a no-regress on throughput. Also require metrics in a dashboard.

joanne: we should also include a GC-style fallback: if free_ratio drops below emergency threshold (e.g., 0.05) trigger a stronger consolidation pass, but rate-limit it and expose a circuit-breaker.

sam.green: added emergency-pass prototype. It runs only when free_ratio < 0.05 and total merge CPU < configured limit. Emergency pass improves mem but is limited to avoid noisy neighbor.

perf-bot: nightly perf job queued for perf-ci-4 with coalescer variants. Results will post here when done. :robot_face:

nate.k: @sam.green please attach the flamegraphs and jeprof diffs to the PR and include the harness command and raw CSVs. I'll review the code and the safety knobs.

sam.green: done — PR updated with jeprof diffs and `flamegraph.svg` links. Also included a small doc on heuristics and knobs.

ravi.s: LGTM in principle. After we get stress runs and perf checks, we can ship buddy coalescer as a low-risk improvement and keep relocate behind opt-in for Dedicated. Also add schema migration notes if we add the 2KB class.

joanne: agreed. add customer-facing notes for Dedicated onboarding (what CPU commit implies).

sam.green: will finalize tests and push for review tomorrow. Thanks all.

(thumbs up reactions and a few quick emojis omitted)
